artists.biography: The Soundtrack of Our Lives, often abbreviated T.S.O.O.L., is a Swedish rock band that was formed in Gothenburg in 1995 and disbanded in 2012. All lyrics are sung in English. The band's style draws heavily on sixties and seventies punk and rock, such as Rolling Stones and Iggy and the Stooges. Psychedelic rock forms another strong influence, and psychedelic and mystical references are also prominent in the band's lyrics and aesthethics. The abbreviation 'OEOC', which features on all their albums, refers to the phrase "as above, so below" from Hermeticism.

perplexity.description:
Welcome to the Infant Freebase is the 1996 debut album by Swedish rock band The Soundtrack of Our Lives, a sprawling 20-track collection spanning over 70 minutes that announces the band's ambitious approach to rock music. The album draws liberally from rock's rich history, channeling influences ranging from classic psychedelia to contemporary indie rock. Tracks like "Instant Repeater '99" evoke the anthemic power of Guided By Voices, while "Embryonic Rendezvous" recalls the dreamy textures of The Beatles' "Strawberry Fields," and "Magic Muslims" channels the dark grandeur of The Rolling Stones' "Paint It Black." The band demonstrates technical proficiency and an eclectic sensibility, treating rock's greatest moments as a toolkit for their own creative expression.

The album's sheer length and density of material reflect TSOOL's uncompromising vision, though this ambition occasionally works against accessibility. Despite the band's years of struggle to secure North American distribution, the album eventually gained recognition as a powerful statement of intent. It established the foundation for their subsequent work, including their 1998 follow-up Extended Revelation, which would shift toward a mellower psychedelic pop approach with greater emphasis on acoustic arrangements and refined songwriting. Welcome to the Infant Freebase remains a testament to a band committed to exploring rock's possibilities without restraint, capturing their raw energy and wide-ranging musical appetite at their creative inception.
